question: Under the National Health Mission the trained female community health activist who links the village community with the health system is the:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. accredited social health activist

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The accredited social health activist, or ASHA, is a village woman chosen by the community and trained to act as the first link between the people and the health services

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — auxiliary nurse midwife: The auxiliary nurse midwife is a government functionary posted at the sub-centre

C — anganwadi worker: The anganwadi worker belongs to the child development services and looks after nutrition and pre-school activities

D — multipurpose health worker: The multipurpose health worker is a salaried male worker of the health department

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: The ASHA is not a paid employee but receives performance based incentives, which is why her motivation and supervision need continued support

question: The multipurpose health worker, male, in a sub-centre area is mainly responsible for:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. vector control measures, sanitation and health education in the villages

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The male worker carries out insecticide spraying, source reduction of mosquito breeding, sanitation and health education in his area

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — conducting normal deliveries: Conducting deliveries is the work of the auxiliary nurse midwife

B — maintaining the sub-centre drug stock: The drug stock at the sub-centre is kept by the auxiliary nurse midwife

D — giving all childhood vaccines: Routine immunisation is mainly carried out by the auxiliary nurse midwife

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: In malarial and filarial areas the timely spraying and larvicidal work of the male worker decides the success of the whole vector control programme
option_3: vector control measures, sanitation and health education in the villages

question: Routine immunisation of children in a sub-centre area is the responsibility of the:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. auxiliary nurse midwife

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The auxiliary nurse midwife conducts the immunisation sessions, maintains the cold chain and keeps the records of the eligible children

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — anganwadi helper: The anganwadi helper assists with food and pre-school care

B — school teacher: The teacher may motivate parents but does not immunise

D — village watchman: The village watchman has no health duty

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: The due list of children is prepared from the sub-centre register, and the ASHA informs the families so that no child is missed

question: An ASHA is generally expected to serve a population of about:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. 1000 persons, that is around 200 to 250 households

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The norm is roughly one ASHA for every thousand rural population, covering about two hundred to two hundred and fifty households

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — one entire block: A block covers a population of about one lakh

B — 10,000 persons: Ten thousand persons cover a whole primary health centre area

C — 100 persons: A hundred persons would make the number of ASHAs unmanageable

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: In tribal, hilly and desert areas a smaller population is allotted to each ASHA because of the distances involved
option_4: 1000 persons, that is around 200 to 250 households

question: An ASHA finds a 3-year-old child in her village with a cough and fast breathing. The correct sequence of her action is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. count the breaths, give the pre-referral dose of the drug from her kit if the child has pneumonia, refer the child to the health centre and follow up

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The ASHA is trained to count the respiratory rate, give the first dose of the pre-referral drug, arrange referral and then follow up to see that the child has been treated

🔍 Key Clues: 3-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — ask the family to buy an antibiotic from the shop: Self medication from a shop wastes money and delays proper treatment

B — refer the child without doing anything else and stop following up: A referral without the pre-referral dose and without follow-up fails the purpose of training

C — give the child a home remedy and wait for three days: Acute respiratory infection in a young child can worsen within hours

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: Counting breaths for a full minute while the child is calm is the finding that decides whether the child needs an antibiotic
option_1: ask the family to buy an antibiotic from the shop
option_2: refer the child without doing anything else and stop following up
option_3: give the child a home remedy and wait for three days
option_4: count the breaths, give the pre-referral dose of the drug from her kit if the child has pneumonia, refer the child to the health centre and follow up

question: An ASHA brings a woman in the first stage of labour to the primary health centre and stays with her until she is admitted. This function is best described as the role of the ASHA as:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. a facilitator who arranges and accompanies the woman for institutional care

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The ASHA mobilises the family, arranges transport and accompanies the woman so that she reaches the facility in time, which is her main contribution to safe motherhood

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — a doctor's assistant in the labour room: She does not assist in the labour room as a trained professional

B — a birth attendant who conducts the delivery: Conducting deliveries is not a part of her training

D — a person who issues the discharge card: Discharge papers are issued by the facility staff

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: Her alertness about danger signs during pregnancy and labour is what converts an emergency into a safe outcome
option_1: a doctor's assistant in the labour room
option_2: a birth attendant who conducts the delivery
option_3: a facilitator who arranges and accompanies the woman for institutional care
option_4: a person who issues the discharge card

question: An auxiliary nurse midwife finds that a 20-day-old baby in her area has never been registered and has therefore received no vaccine. Her correct action is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. register the birth, give the vaccines that are due for the age after checking, begin the due list and counsel the mother about the remaining schedule

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Registration and catch-up immunisation as per the schedule are the correct steps, and the child is then entered in the due list so that no dose is missed

🔍 Key Clues: 20-day-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — ask the family to go to the district hospital: The sub-centre is the proper place for routine immunisation

B — wait until the child is two months old: Waiting loses the protection for the period of greatest risk

C — give all the vaccines of the first year at once: Giving all the doses together is not permitted and would be unsafe

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: The BCG and the birth dose of the other vaccines are given as soon as the omission is detected, without starting the schedule again
option_1: ask the family to go to the district hospital
option_2: wait until the child is two months old
option_3: give all the vaccines of the first year at once
option_4: register the birth, give the vaccines that are due for the age after checking, begin the due list and counsel the mother about the remaining schedule

question: A woman in her eighth month of pregnancy tells the ASHA that she will deliver at home because her husband is away and there is no one to take her to the hospital. The most useful action of the ASHA is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. explain the risks, identify a birth preparedness plan with a companion, arrange transport and the money in advance and involve the other family members and the panchayat

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Birth preparedness planning identifies the facility, the transport, the funds and a companion beforehand, which is exactly what converts a home delivery plan into an institutional one

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — warn the woman that she will be responsible for any mishap: Threatening the woman destroys trust and changes nothing

C — inform the police: Non compliance with advice is not a police matter

D — accept the decision, as it is the family's choice: Accepting the decision without offering a solution leaves both mother and baby at risk

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: Involving the mother in law and other relatives is often more effective than counselling the woman alone, since the decision is taken by the family
option_1: explain the risks, identify a birth preparedness plan with a companion, arrange transport and the money in advance and involve the other family members and the panchayat
option_2: warn the woman that she will be responsible for any mishap
option_4: accept the decision, as it is the family's choice

question: The school health services in India provide for:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. health appraisal, immunisation, nutrition and health education, and a safe school environment

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The programme is comprehensive and includes periodic health examination, immunisation, supplementary nutrition, health education and attention to the water supply, toilets and buildings

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — only the annual sports day: Sports is not a health service activity

B — only the treatment of sick children: Treatment is only one of the components

D — only health education: Health education alone cannot correct anaemia or defective vision

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: The health card of every child is maintained in the school so that growth and defects can be followed over the years
option_3: health appraisal, immunisation, nutrition and health education, and a safe school environment

question: A 9-year-old school child is found to have a haemoglobin of 9 grams per decilitre and says that he eats only rice and pickle for lunch. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. give deworming treatment and iron and folic acid as per the programme, teach the family about a balanced, iron rich diet and review him on the next visit

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Deworming, supplementation and dietary counselling together correct anaemia, and he also needs a check for other causes if the value does not improve

🔍 Key Clues: 9-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — send him home for a month: Sending him home does not treat the cause and interrupts his schooling

B — advise only a tonic from the market: Market tonics are costly and not needed when the programme supplies iron and folic acid free

C — report the family to the authorities: The family has no case to answer and reporting would destroy the relationship

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: The child's lunch habit is discussed with the mother and with the teacher, since a mid-day meal often supplies the only balanced meal of the day
option_2: advise only a tonic from the market
option_4: give deworming treatment and iron and folic acid as per the programme, teach the family about a balanced, iron rich diet and review him on the next visit

question: Under the national programme, deworming with albendazole is carried out in schools:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. for all eligible children on a fixed deworming day, after excluding the very young, the sick and those with a known allergy

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Mass deworming is given on a fixed day to all eligible children, since the worm load cannot be judged by appearance alone

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — only for girls: Boys are equally affected by worm infestation

C — only for children who look pale: Pale children do not represent the whole group at risk

D — every month throughout the year: Monthly treatment is unnecessary and is not the schedule

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: The child is given the tablet at school in the presence of the teacher so that it is actually swallowed and any immediate reaction is noticed
option_1: for all eligible children on a fixed deworming day, after excluding the very young, the sick and those with a known allergy

question: Four children of a primary school develop jaundice within one week and all of them drink water from an unprotected open tank in the school compound. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. inform the health authority at once, examine the water source and the toilets, search for further cases, arrange safe drinking water and teach hand hygiene

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A cluster of jaundice suggests water borne hepatitis or another enteric infection, and the response is notification, source investigation, case search and immediate water and hygiene measures

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — close the school permanently: Permanent closure is unnecessary and disrupts education

B — give antibiotics to all the children: Antibiotics have no role in a viral or water borne outbreak

C — ask the affected children to stay at home for two months: Long exclusion of the affected children does not stop transmission from the source

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: The incubation period of hepatitis is long, so cases appear for several weeks after the source is corrected, which is explained to the school staff
option_3: ask the affected children to stay at home for two months
option_4: inform the health authority at once, examine the water source and the toilets, search for further cases, arrange safe drinking water and teach hand hygiene

question: In health education for adolescent school girls, which topic deserves the highest priority?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. menstrual hygiene, nutrition with iron and folic acid, and the prevention of anaemia

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Poor menstrual hygiene and anaemia are the two commonest problems of adolescent girls, and both are correctable by simple education and supplementation

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — the history of nursing: The history of nursing does not address an adolescent health need

B — the use of cosmetics: Cosmetics have little health value

D — the rules of cricket: Games are useful but not the first health priority

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: Educating boys as well as girls about menstrual hygiene reduces teasing and improves school attendance of girls
option_3: menstrual hygiene, nutrition with iron and folic acid, and the prevention of anaemia

question: Under the Factories Act, the pre-placement medical examination is compulsory for a worker who is to be employed in:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. a hazardous process or in a job involving exposure to a health hazard

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The Act requires a pre-placement examination and periodic re-examination of every worker employed in a hazardous process, so that the baseline health status is known

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — the office section: Office workers are not employed in a hazardous process

C — the security section: Security work does not involve a health hazard as defined

D — the canteen: The canteen is not a hazardous process

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: The baseline record is what later allows an occupational disease to be attributed to the workplace and compensation to be claimed
option_2: a hazardous process or in a job involving exposure to a health hazard

question: Byssinosis, also called Monday fever, occurs in workers exposed to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. cotton dust

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Byssinosis results from inhaling cotton, flax or hemp dust, and the characteristic chest tightness appears on the first day of the working week

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — asbestos: Asbestos causes asbestosis and mesothelioma

B — silica dust: Silica causes silicosis

D — coal dust: Coal dust causes coal worker's pneumoconiosis and melanosis

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: Dust control by exhaust ventilation and wet methods is the only measure that truly prevents this disease

question: A 45-year-old worker in a textile mill complains of breathlessness and tightness in the chest on the first day of the week, and the symptoms improve over the next two days. He has no fever and his chest is clear on examination. The most likely condition is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. byssinosis due to cotton dust

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The classic pattern of symptoms appearing on the first working day and improving during the week is characteristic of byssinosis from cotton dust

🔍 Key Clues: 45-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — pneumonia: Pneumonia is an acute febrile illness with local signs on examination

B — bronchial asthma of allergic origin: Asthma is not tied to the first day of the week and usually has an atopic history

C — pulmonary tuberculosis: Tuberculosis gives fever, weight loss and evening rise of temperature, along with shadows on the film

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: Continued exposure leads to permanent airflow obstruction, so the worker must be moved away from the dust area at this stage

question: The most effective measure to prevent noise induced hearing loss in a factory is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. control the noise at its source by enclosing or damping the machine, along with hearing protection and periodic audiometry

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Engineering control at the source removes the hazard, and protection, monitoring and education complete the programme

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — increase the speed of the machine to shorten the exposure: A faster machine is usually noisier

B — rotate the workers between noisy areas: Rotation spreads the risk to more workers instead of reducing it

D — issue ear plugs to all the workers and take no other step: Ear plugs alone depend on correct, continuous use and often fail

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: Periodic audiometry detects the earliest fall in hearing at high frequencies, when a change of job can still prevent serious loss
option_1: increase the speed of the machine to shorten the exposure
option_3: control the noise at its source by enclosing or damping the machine, along with hearing protection and periodic audiometry
option_4: issue ear plugs to all the workers and take no other step

question: A 38-year-old worker in a battery factory has a blood lead level well above the permissible limit and complains of colicky abdominal pain. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. remove him from further exposure, inform the factory medical officer, arrange chelation treatment as advised and get the workplace inspected

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Lead absorption needs to be stopped at the source, and the affected worker must be taken out of exposure and treated under medical advice

🔍 Key Clues: 38-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — tell him to eat more iron rich food and continue in the same job: More iron in the diet does not remove lead from the body or from the workplace, and continued exposure worsens the poisoning

B — advise him to wear gloves while working: Gloves protect the skin but not against inhaled lead fume and dust

C — give him a painkiller and send him back to work: A painkiller masks the symptom and allows the absorption to go on

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: Colicky abdominal pain with constipation and anaemia in a battery worker is a classical picture of lead poisoning and needs an urgent blood lead estimation
option_1: tell him to eat more iron rich food and continue in the same job
option_2: advise him to wear gloves while working
option_3: give him a painkiller and send him back to work
option_4: remove him from further exposure, inform the factory medical officer, arrange chelation treatment as advised and get the workplace inspected

question: In a mass casualty incident the first action of the nurse at the site is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. triage the casualties and attend first to those who need immediate life saving care

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Triage sorts the casualties by the severity of injury and the chance of survival, so that the limited staff and supplies are used where they save the most lives

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — give first aid to the casualty who is nearest: Attending to whoever is nearest wastes the golden hour on those who can wait

B — shift every injured person to hospital at once: Moving all the injured together overloads the hospital and delays treatment of the serious cases

C — wait for the ambulances to arrive before touching anyone: Waiting without giving any care loses lives that could be saved by simple measures

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: During triage only simple life saving measures such as clearing the airway and controlling bleeding are given, and definitive treatment comes later
option_1: give first aid to the casualty who is nearest
option_2: shift every injured person to hospital at once
option_3: wait for the ambulances to arrive before touching anyone
option_4: triage the casualties and attend first to those who need immediate life saving care

question: In disaster triage a casualty is labelled red. This label means that the casualty:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. needs immediate life saving treatment to survive

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The red label marks the highest priority group, whose injuries are life threatening but can be saved by immediate treatment

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — has only minor injuries and can walk: Walking casualties with minor injuries are labelled green

B — has injuries that can wait for a few hours: Those who can wait are labelled yellow

D — is dead or has injuries beyond any help: Casualties beyond help are labelled black

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse re-examines the labelled casualties at intervals because the condition of a casualty can change from yellow to red while he waits
option_1: has only minor injuries and can walk
option_2: has injuries that can wait for a few hours
option_3: needs immediate life saving treatment to survive
option_4: is dead or has injuries beyond any help

question: In a relief camp set up after a flood there is a sudden rise in cases of acute diarrhoea. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. check and chlorinate the drinking water, correct the toilets and waste disposal, treat the patients with oral rehydration, separate the severe cases and inform the health authority

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Diarrhoea in a relief camp is almost always water or food borne, so the water source, the sanitation and the case management are attended to together

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — stop the supply of water to the camp altogether: Stopping the water supply without an alternative causes dehydration in the whole camp

C — ask all the families to leave the camp: Dispersing the families spreads the infection to new areas and leaves the sick without care

D — give antibiotics to every person in the camp: Mass medication is not needed and breeds resistance

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: A single stool sample from a few patients is enough to identify the organism, and oral rehydration corners are set up immediately
option_1: stop the supply of water to the camp altogether
option_2: check and chlorinate the drinking water, correct the toilets and waste disposal, treat the patients with oral rehydration, separate the severe cases and inform the health authority
option_3: ask all the families to leave the camp
option_4: give antibiotics to every person in the camp

question: Community training, mock drills and the pre-positioning of emergency supplies belong to which phase of disaster management?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. preparedness

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Preparedness includes all the measures taken before a disaster to ensure an effective response, such as training, drills, planning and stockpiling

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — rehabilitation: Rehabilitation restores normal life in the period after the emergency

C — mitigation: Mitigation reduces the impact of a hazard in the long term, for example by building codes and flood embankments

D — response: The response phase covers the emergency work done during and immediately after the event

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: A community that has practised a drill evacuates in minutes, while an unprepared one loses hours

question: In sociology the family is best described as:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. a universal social institution based on marriage and kinship that cares for its members from birth to death

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The family is the basic and universal institution, founded on marriage and kinship, and it performs biological, economic, socialising and protective functions

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — a group of people of the same age: A group of the same age is a peer group

C — an association of neighbours: Neighbours form a neighbourhood and not a family

D — a temporary arrangement for sharing a house: The family is not temporary and is not merely a housing arrangement

⚠️ Exam Trap: Do not pick an option only because it is familiar - the option that fits the whole stem is the answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: Because the family decides about food, treatment and care, the community nurse works with the family rather than with the individual alone
option_1: a universal social institution based on marriage and kinship that cares for its members from birth to death
option_2: a group of people of the same age
option_4: a temporary arrangement for sharing a house

question: Which social factor most strongly influences the use of maternal health services by women in rural India?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. the education of the woman and her participation in decisions about her own health

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Education raises awareness of danger signs and of the value of antenatal care, and a woman who takes part in decisions is far more likely to use the services

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — the number of festivals celebrated in the village: Festivals may delay a visit but do not explain the difference between families

C — the number of relatives living in the village: The number of relatives has no direct effect on the use of services

D — the size of the family house: The size of the house does not determine health behaviour

⚠️ Exam Trap: Do not pick an option only because it is familiar - the option that fits the whole stem is the answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: This is why girls' education is treated as a health intervention in its own right
option_1: the education of the woman and her participation in decisions about her own health
option_2: the number of festivals celebrated in the village
option_3: the number of relatives living in the village

question: During a home visit the nurse learns that the family follows a tradition of not giving green leafy vegetables to a pregnant woman in the last months. The most useful approach is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. listen to the belief with respect, explain the need for iron and calcium in simple terms and suggest locally available substitutes in a form the family will accept

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A belief that is ridiculed is not given up, whereas one that is understood and gently modified usually changes, and substitutes preserve the nutritional need

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — report the family to the panchayat: The family has broken no rule and reporting would end the nurse's usefulness in that house

C — tell the family firmly that the practice is wrong and harmful: A firm order invites resistance and the woman continues as before

D — give iron tablets and say nothing about the diet: Ignoring the diet leaves a large gap in the intake, since tablets alone cannot meet the need

⚠️ Exam Trap: Look for the qualifier (FIRST / BEST / MOST LIKELY) - it decides the answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The reason behind such a belief is usually a fear of a large baby or of a difficult delivery, and answering that fear is the key to change
option_1: listen to the belief with respect, explain the need for iron and calcium in simple terms and suggest locally available substitutes in a form the family will accept
option_3: tell the family firmly that the practice is wrong and harmful
option_4: give iron tablets and say nothing about the diet

question: The first step in the research process is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. identify and state the research problem

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A clearly stated problem and objective decide what will be studied, how and with what tools, so it comes first

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — collect the data: Data collection follows the design and the selection of tools

C — analyse the data: Analysis is done only after the data are collected

D — write the final report: The report is the last stage of the study

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: A problem that is too broad cannot be answered by one study, so it is narrowed down until it can be measured

question: The section of a research report that presents what is already known about the problem is the:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. review of literature

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The review of literature summarises earlier work, shows the gap that this study fills and supports the choice of the design

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — methodology: Methodology describes how the study was carried out

C — results: Results present the findings of this study

D — conclusion: The conclusion states what can be inferred from the findings

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: A review that is limited to a few old references weakens the whole study, as the researcher may be repeating work already done

question: A nurse researcher wishes to record the hand hygiene practice of the staff as it actually occurs during work. The most suitable tool is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. a structured observation checklist

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Observation records what people actually do, whereas the other methods record what they say they do, and hand hygiene is well known to be over reported

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — an opinion poll: An opinion poll records views and not actions

B — a questionnaire: A questionnaire depends on the respondent's memory and honesty

C — a personal interview: An interview has the same weakness as the questionnaire in this situation

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: The observer standing in the ward may itself change the practice, so the observation is repeated over several days and shifts

question: The mean, the median and the mode are all measures of:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. central tendency

🧠 Clinical Rationale: All three describe the central value around which the observations cluster

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — correlation: Correlation measures the association between two variables

B — probability: Probability is the chance of an event occurring

D — dispersion: Dispersion is described by the range, the variance and the standard deviation

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: Reporting the mean alone hides the spread, so the standard deviation or the range is always given with it

question: A researcher measures the pain score of the same twenty patients before and after an intervention. The appropriate test of significance is the:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. paired t test

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The same subjects are measured twice, so the two sets of readings are related and the paired t test is used

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — chi square test: The chi square test compares observed and expected frequencies in categories

C — coefficient of correlation: A correlation coefficient describes the strength of an association and does not test a difference

D — unpaired t test: The unpaired t test compares two independent groups

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

question: The median is preferred to the mean as a measure of central tendency when:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. the data contain extreme values or are skewed

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The median is the middle value and is not affected by a few very large or very small readings, so it represents a skewed distribution better

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — the data are perfectly symmetrical: With symmetrical data the median and the mean nearly coincide, so nothing is gained

B — the data are only categorical: Categorical data are summarised by the mode and by proportions

C — every observation is identical: If all values are identical, every measure of central tendency has the same value

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: The average length of stay in a ward is usually reported as the median, because one patient staying for months would pull the mean upwards
option_4: the data contain extreme values or are skewed

question: Among the following the richest source of vitamin C is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. amla

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The Indian gooseberry, or amla, contains a very high amount of vitamin C and is the cheapest local source

❌ Why Not Other Options?

question: A 2-year-old child admitted with severe acute malnutrition has been treated for low blood sugar and hypothermia. After stabilisation the first feed is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. F-75 therapeutic milk in small frequent feeds

🧠 Clinical Rationale: F-75 is a low protein, low energy starter formula given in small frequent feeds, and F-100 or a ready to use therapeutic food is introduced only after the appetite returns

🔍 Key Clues: 2-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

⚠️ Exam Trap: Separate the deficiency disease from its dietary source - exams mix the two.

question: The absorption of iron from a vegetarian meal is best improved by taking with it:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. a source of vitamin C such as lemon or guava

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Vitamin C converts the iron to the ferrous form and forms a soluble complex, which increases its absorption considerably

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — tea: Tannins in tea bind iron and reduce its absorption

C — wheat bran: Phytates in bran bind iron and reduce its absorption

D — a cup of milk: The calcium in milk competes with iron and reduces its absorption

⚠️ Exam Trap: Separate the deficiency disease from its dietary source - exams mix the two.

💎 PNC Pearl: Iron tablets are given with lemon water or citrus fruit and away from tea and milk for the same reason
option_1: a source of vitamin C such as lemon or guava

question: The additional energy requirement of a woman during the second half of pregnancy is about:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. 300 kilocalories per day

🧠 Clinical Rationale: An extra three hundred kilocalories a day is recommended in the second half of pregnancy, along with extra protein, iron, calcium and folic acid

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — 1000 kilocalories per day: A thousand extra kilocalories is far beyond the need and would cause excessive weight gain

C — 600 kilocalories per day: Six hundred kilocalories is about the extra need during lactation and not in pregnancy

D — 100 kilocalories per day: A hundred kilocalories is too little to support the growth of the fetus and the maternal tissues

⚠️ Exam Trap: In obstetric questions ask who is at immediate risk, mother or fetus - that decides the first action.

question: To reduce the loss of B vitamins while preparing rice, the correct practice is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. wash it in a small quantity of water and cook it with just enough water so that no water is left to be drained off

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The B vitamins are water soluble and sit near the surface of the grain, so repeated washing and draining of the cooking water removes a large part of them

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — soak it overnight and pour away the water: Overnight soaking and discarding the water has the same effect

C — wash the rice many times in a large quantity of water and throw the water away: Many washings in excess water wash away the vitamins and part of the protein

D — cook it in plenty of water and drain the excess water: Drained cooking water carries away the vitamins with it

⚠️ Exam Trap: Separate the deficiency disease from its dietary source - exams mix the two.

💎 PNC Pearl: Polishing removes the outer layers of the grain, so parboiled and unpolished rice retain more of these vitamins

question: A 60-year-old man who is taking warfarin asks about his diet. The nurse should advise him to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. keep his intake of vitamin K rich foods such as green leafy vegetables steady and to avoid sudden large changes, and to attend for the blood tests

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Warfarin acts by blocking vitamin K, so it is the consistency of the intake that matters, and the dose is adjusted according to the blood test result

🔍 Key Clues: 60-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — double the dose of warfarin on the days when he eats greens: Changing the dose without a blood test can cause bleeding or a clot

B — take a vitamin K tablet every day: Added vitamin K would oppose the drug and reduce its effect

D — avoid green leafy vegetables completely for the rest of his life: Complete avoidance is neither necessary nor practical and leads to a poor diet

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The patient is warned to report at once any unusual bleeding, bruising or black stools

question: Honey should not be given to an infant below one year of age because it may contain:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. Clostridium botulinum spores

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The immature gut of an infant allows the spores of Clostridium botulinum to germinate and produce toxin, causing infantile botulism with constipation, weak cry and poor feeding

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — hepatitis A virus: Hepatitis A is also spread by contaminated food and water

B — Entamoeba histolytica: Amoebiasis is spread by contaminated food and water

C — Salmonella typhi: Typhoid is spread by contaminated food and water and is not linked to honey

⚠️ Exam Trap: In paediatric questions look at the age first - the normal values and the expected action change with age.

💎 PNC Pearl: Honey is safe after one year of age, when the intestinal flora and the immune defences have matured

question: The normal oral temperature of a healthy adult is about:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. 37 degrees Celsius

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The normal oral temperature is about thirty seven degrees Celsius, or ninety eight point six degrees Fahrenheit

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 35 degrees Celsius: Thirty five degrees is hypothermia

D — 39 degrees Celsius: Thirty nine degrees is fever

question: Before recording an oral temperature the nurse should ask the patient to:
solution:

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — take a hot drink to warm the mouth: A hot drink raises the reading falsely

⚠️ Exam Trap: In procedure questions choose the step that protects the patient first - safety before comfort and speed.

question: A 70-year-old patient receiving intravenous fluids develops pain and swelling around the cannula site with cool skin and a slowed drip rate. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. stop the infusion, remove the cannula, elevate the limb, apply the prescribed cold compress and record the event

🧠 Clinical Rationale: These are the signs of infiltration, and the infusion must be stopped at once, the cannula removed and the limb elevated, with a cold compress for the first day

🔍 Key Clues: 70-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — increase the drip rate to clear the line: Increasing the rate pushes more fluid into the tissues and worsens the swelling

C — apply a warm pack and continue the same infusion: Continuing the infusion through the same cannula is unsafe, and warmth is used only after the first day

D — massage the site to disperse the fluid: Massage spreads the fluid and may cause further damage

⚠️ Exam Trap: In procedure questions choose the step that protects the patient first - safety before comfort and speed.

💎 PNC Pearl: A new cannula is inserted in the opposite limb, and the site is inspected at every shift in an elderly patient, whose veins are fragile

question: The correct technique for measuring capillary blood glucose is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. clean the finger, let it dry, prick the side of the fingertip and use a hanging drop without squeezing

question: A patient with chronic constipation should be advised to take:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. a high fibre diet with plenty of fluids and regular exercise

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Fibre adds bulk, fluid softens the stool and activity stimulates peristalsis, which together restore normal bowel function

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — strong purgatives every day: Habitual purgatives make the bowel dependent on them

B — only milk and milk products: Milk alone does not provide the fibre needed

C — a low residue diet with less fluid: A low residue diet and reduced fluids make the stool harder

⚠️ Exam Trap: Separate the deficiency disease from its dietary source - exams mix the two.

option_4: a high fibre diet with plenty of fluids and regular exercise

question: After a lumbar puncture the patient is advised to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. lie flat for the period advised by the doctor, with adequate fluids

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Lying flat reduces the leakage of cerebrospinal fluid, which is the main cause of the headache that follows the procedure

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — take a hot bath: A hot bath has no relation to the complication

B — do deep breathing exercises while standing: Standing exercises bring on the headache

C — sit up immediately and walk about: Sitting or standing up soon after increases the risk of a post puncture headache

⚠️ Exam Trap: In procedure questions choose the step that protects the patient first - safety before comfort and speed.

option_4: lie flat for the period advised by the doctor, with adequate fluids

question: A 58-year-old woman has sudden severe headache with drooping of the left side of the face and weakness of the left arm. Her blood pressure is 190/110 mm Hg. The nurse's priority action is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. keep her lying with the head slightly raised, check the consciousness, pupils and vital signs, give nothing by mouth and arrange immediate transfer to a hospital with a scan facility

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The sudden onset of focal weakness with a severe headache suggests a stroke, and a scan is needed to tell bleeding from blockage; nothing is given by mouth until swallowing is assessed

🔍 Key Clues: 58-year-old | 110 mm

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — give her a tablet for headache and let her rest: Rest and a painkiller lose the time in which treatment can limit the brain damage

B — make her walk to assess the weakness: Making her walk risks a fall and further injury

C — give her a hot drink to settle her: A hot drink risks aspiration, as swallowing is often affected in a stroke

⚠️ Exam Trap: Look for the qualifier (FIRST / BEST / MOST LIKELY) - it decides the answer.

question: The correct first aid for a sprained ankle in the first twenty four hours is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. rest, ice, compression and elevation

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Cold reduces bleeding and swelling, compression limits the collection of fluid and elevation helps it to drain

❌ Why Not Other Options?

D — hot fomentation and massage: Heat and massage increase the bleeding into the tissue

question: Which set of findings in a patient with dengue fever requires immediate admission?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. persistent vomiting, severe abdominal pain, bleeding from the gums and cold clammy extremities

question: A 62-year-old man with an indwelling urinary catheter has a temperature of 39 degrees Celsius with cloudy, foul smelling urine. The nurse should:

question: The cuff pressure of a tracheostomy tube should generally be kept at about:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. 20 to 25 centimetres of water

question: The third stage of labour is the period from the birth of the baby to the:

question: Under the national programme the drug given routinely to the mother immediately after delivery to prevent postpartum haemorrhage is:
solution:

question: Thirty minutes after a normal delivery a woman has a pulse of 112 per minute and a boggy uterus, and there is a trickle of blood. The nurse should:

question: The Moro reflex is normally present at birth and disappears by about:
solution:

question: A normal infant is usually able to sit without support at about:

question: A 6-month-old infant has not gained weight for two months and is being given diluted cow's milk in a bottle. The nurse should advise the mother to:

question: The drug of choice in an acute attack of anaphylaxis is:
solution:

question: The normal pH of arterial blood is:
solution:

question: The part of the brain that regulates the body temperature is the:
solution:

question: Which change on the electrocardiogram suggests a raised serum potassium level?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. tall, peaked T waves

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Hyperkalaemia makes the myocardium repolarise abnormally, producing tall, tented T waves, and the change can progress to a widened QRS and cardiac arrest

❌ Why Not Other Options?

question: The most appropriate initial approach to a withdrawn patient who sits alone and avoids speech is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. sit quietly near him, make a simple opening remark and allow silence

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A calm presence with brief, simple openings gives the patient time and shows that he is accepted, and silence gives him space to respond

question: A 32-year-old man with schizophrenia stopped his medicine three months ago and now talks to himself, has not slept for three nights and refuses food. The priority action of the nurse is to:
solution:

🔍 Key Clues: 32-year-old

question: The commonest organism causing urinary tract infection in women is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. Escherichia coli

question: The death of an area of tissue because of loss of its blood supply is called:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. infarction

question: A registered nurse delegates the recording of vital signs to a nursing student. The nurse remains responsible for:
solution:

question: In a non-diabetic adult the blood glucose two hours after a seventy five gram oral glucose load should be:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. below 140 milligrams per decilitre

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A two hour value below one hundred and forty milligrams per decilitre is taken as normal, between one hundred and forty and two hundred as impaired tolerance, and above two hundred as diabetes in a symptomatic person

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — above 250 milligrams per decilitre: A value above two hundred and fifty is clearly abnormal

C — above 200 milligrams per decilitre: A value above two hundred is diagnostic of diabetes and not normal

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

question: In Maslow's hierarchy of needs, which need comes immediately after the physiological needs?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. safety and security

question: Down syndrome is caused by the presence of an extra copy of chromosome:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. 21

question: World No Tobacco Day is observed every year on:

question: The national programme for the prevention and control of cancer, diabetes, cardiovascular diseases and stroke is known by the abbreviation:

question: The main objective of the Swachh Bharat Mission (Gramin) is to:

question: The Fit India Movement was launched in the year:

question: The Indian state with the largest tribal population is:

question: The Kayakalp award scheme of the health ministry is given for:

question: The instrument used to measure the humidity of the air is the:

question: The inert gas filled in an electric bulb to prevent the filament from burning is:

question: The length of the small intestine in an adult is about:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. 6 metres

question: Quinine, used in the treatment of malaria, is obtained from the:

question: The oral polio vaccine used in the immunisation programme contains:
solution:

question: Disposable syringes and surgical gloves are sterilised in industry by:

question: The chemical name of common bleaching powder is:
solution:

question: The law which states that the solubility of a gas in a liquid is directly proportional to the partial pressure of the gas is:
solution:

question: The average of 5, 10, 15, 20 and 25 is:
solution:

question: A health centre attends to 4500 patients in a month and about 40 percent of them are children. The number of children seen is:

question: Fifteen percent of the population of a village of 8000 persons is above sixty years of age. The number of elderly persons is:

question: Which of the following fractions is the largest?

question: The population of a village was 12,000 in 2020 and has grown by 5 percent every year. Its population in 2022 is:

question: A nurse walks 3 kilometres towards the east and then 4 kilometres towards the north. How far is she from the starting point?

💎 PNC Trick: Working letter by letter without hurrying is the same discipline needed when transcribing a drug name that looks like another

question: Ravi is taller than Suresh, Suresh is taller than Kamal, and Mahesh is taller than Ravi. Who is the shortest?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. Kamal

🧠 Method: The order from the tallest is Mahesh, Ravi, Suresh and then Kamal, so Kamal is the shortest

⚡ Fast Approach: Positions add up to one more than the total number in the row.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Ravi: Ravi is taller than both Suresh and Kamal

C — Mahesh: Mahesh is the tallest of all four

D — Suresh: Suresh is taller than Kamal

⚠️ Exam Trap: In FIRST-action questions, identify the life-threatening problem and stabilise or assess before anything else.

💎 PNC Trick: Arranging the given facts in a single order before answering avoids the common error of jumping to a conclusion

question: If the first of January in a certain year is a Sunday, what day of the week is the first of February in that year?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. Wednesday

🧠 Method: January has thirty one days, and thirty one divided by seven leaves a remainder of three, so the day moves three places ahead from Sunday to Wednesday

⚡ Fast Approach: Use the remainder after dividing by 7 for days, and 30 degrees per hour for clocks.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Thursday: Thursday would be four days ahead

C — Tuesday: Tuesday would be only two days ahead

D — Monday: Monday would be one day ahead

⚠️ Exam Trap: Look for the qualifier (FIRST / BEST / MOST LIKELY) - it decides the answer.

💎 PNC Trick: The day of the week is recorded on every prescription and order, so accurate reckoning of dates prevents a drug being given on the wrong day

question: Some patients are diabetic. All diabetic patients need diet control. Which conclusion follows?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. some patients need diet control

🧠 Method: Since some patients are diabetic and every diabetic needs diet control, those patients certainly need it

⚡ Fast Approach: Draw the circles of the given sets and see which conclusion is certain.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — no patient needs diet control: The opposite conclusion is drawn from the given statements

C — only diabetic patients who are admitted need diet control: Admission is not mentioned in the statements

D — all patients need diet control: Only some patients are diabetic, so the conclusion about all patients does not follow

⚠️ Exam Trap: Be careful with absolute words such as ALWAYS and NEVER unless the fact is truly absolute.

💎 PNC Trick: Reasoning from what is actually stated, and not from what seems likely, is the basis of sound clinical judgement

question: A clock gains five minutes in every hour. If it is set right at eight in the morning, what time will it show at eight in the evening of the same day?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. nine in the night

🧠 Method: In twelve hours the clock gains five minutes each hour, that is sixty minutes, so it shows nine in the night when the correct time is eight

⚡ Fast Approach: Use the remainder after dividing by 7 for days, and 30 degrees per hour for clocks.

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — seven in the night: A loss of time is not described here

C — eight in the night: No gain at all would leave it at eight

D — eight thirty in the night: Half an hour of gain would need only six hours

⚠️ Exam Trap: In FIRST-action questions, identify the life-threatening problem and stabilise or assess before anything else.
